correctness.rationale: For p not dividing b, normalization gives independent digit contributions in directions (b^j,b^-j). These lie on y=x modulo p^u; v_0 and v_1 generate that entire subgroup since v_1-b^-1 v_0 generates its first-coordinate difference ideal. This includes the diagonal case u=a. Unrestricted positions contain linearly many periods of directions; every nontrivial subgroup character contracts on at least one occurring direction by the availability of digits 0 and 1. The possibly length-dependent leading-digit contribution has modulus at most one. Fourier inversion gives exponential mixing for fixed b,p,a (also when b=1 modulo p^a and the period is one). The zero pair is unchanged by removing normalization. For p dividing b, h=ceil(a/e) digits at each end suffice and are disjoint as soon as ell>=2h. The low block is uniform modulo p^a. Reverse divisibility requires the leading digit to be a multiple of p^min(a,e); there are b/p^min(a,e)-1 such permitted digits. If a>e, the next h-1 digits then meet one uniform congruence modulo p^(a-e), since b/p^e is a unit and p^(a-e) divides b^(h-1). The valuation pmf follows by subtracting adjacent tails, including t=0 and t=tau. An independently implemented raw-residue exact DP confirmed 27 stabilization cases and seven support/total-variation comparisons.
residual_risks: Mixing is for each fixed modulus; finite DP does not establish the rate or a uniform-in-modulus bound.
The exact p-divides-b bound is a sufficient cutoff; optimality for every parameter is not claimed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The global binary sieve is stronger for a different statistic, not an arbitrary base/modulus joint-residue law. Palindromic inputs satisfy R=N by assumption; their residue distribution does not imply the arbitrary-input paired law. Cyclic rotation is not reversal.

evidence: Binary mod 9 at p=3 is a genuine match: each marginal zero mass is 1/9 and common zero mass is 1/27, consistent with avoiding both zeros with probability 22/27. The cited main theorem is for joint squarefreeness, not the full fixed-power law.
The general dependence ideal in the audited proof is generated by b-b^-1; the separate low/high digit-block argument is needed in the nonunit case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The previous special cases do not give the subgroup y=x modulo p^min(a,v_p(b²−1)) for arbitrary fixed a, nor the exact cutoff for p|b. Standard finite Fourier mixing is not claimed as new.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The database records establish the statistic and special congruences, but do not supply joint subgroup sizes, the limiting local probabilities or the base-divisor stabilization. This is a bounded comparison, not proof of absence.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the all-base fixed-prime-power law: exponential joint mixing on the exact subgroup in the unit case and an exact arbitrary-prime-power cutoff in the nonunit case. Known decimal divisibility rules and binary squarefree/local examples are not credited as novel.
residual_risks: Prior binary and decimal special cases exist, and general finite-group random walk theory is standard.
Bounded searches do not exclude unindexed equivalent all-base results.

value.rationale: The dependence of an integer and its reversal is essential for local gcd factors. This computes the exact dependence subgroup, the transition in the valuation tail, and a concrete finite-length rule for the potentially nonuniform leading digit in the nonunit case. It replaces an independence heuristic with explicit joint probabilities for every fixed prime power.
residual_risks: No global gcd distribution, uniform estimate in growing moduli or cross-prime independence result follows as stated.
